en: Itivuttaka 84:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on the Welfare of the Many.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Three kinds of persons, arising in the world, arise for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans."
Which three?

Here, monks, a Tathāgata arises in the world, an Arahant, a perfectly enlightened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Well-Gone One, a knower of the worlds, an unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life, entirely complete and pure.

“Monks, this is the first person who, arising in the world, arises for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

Furthermore, monks, another disciple of that very Teacher is an arahant, one whose taints are destroyed, who has lived the holy life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is completely liberated through final knowledge.”

He teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life (brahmacariya) in its entirety, perfectly complete and pure.

This, monks, is the second person who arises in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
Furthermore, monks, there is another disciple of that same Teacher who is a trainee (sekha), practicing the path, learned, and established in virtuous conduct.
He too teaches the Dhamma that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing; he reveals the holy life, entirely complete and pure.

This, monks, is the third person who appears in the world for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

“Monks, these three persons, arising in the world, arise for the welfare of many, for the happiness of many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.
Thus spoke the Blessed One. With regard to this, it is said:
“The Teacher is indeed the first great seer in the world;
his follower is the disciple who has developed himself.
Then there is another, the one on the Path, who is still a trainee.”
The one who is learned, the one endowed with virtue, and the one endowed with wisdom—
these three are the best among gods and humans,
illuminators who proclaim the Dhamma.
They open the door to the Deathless;
they liberate many people from the bonds,
those who are led by the unsurpassed Caravan-Leader.
They follow the well-taught path;
those who are heedful in the teaching of the Sugata make an end of suffering right here.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The fifth.
